outline.description: This chapter establishes the factual context of the employment dispute involving overtime pay policies for licensed attorneys, outlines the specific Minnesota state statutes invoked by the plaintiff, and details the unique procedural history where the plaintiff was fully compensated for back wages and liquidated damages prior to the summary judgment motion.
subtopics: Factual background: Consilio's role as a document review firm and the 2019 elimination of premium overtime pay
Statutory framework: Overview of the MPWA, MFLSA, and MWTA claims filed by Cohen
Pre-trial developments: The stipulation that Cohen received all owed overtime wages and liquidated damages
Procedural strategy: Agreement to litigate summary judgment on remaining penalty claims before further discovery

outline.chapter_title: Standard of Review and Analytical Framework
outline.description: This section defines the appellate standard applied to the district court's decision, clarifying how summary judgment is evaluated under federal law while noting the specific requirement to view evidence in the light most favorable to the non-moving party.
subtopics: De novo review standard for grants of summary judgment
The 'no genuine issue of material fact' threshold
Application of Minnesota statutory interpretation principles (plain language rule)
Distinction between compensatory damages available to employees versus civil penalties reserved for the state

outline.chapter_title: Analysis of MPWA Claim: Private Right to Penalties
outline.description: This chapter examines whether an individual employee can sue for 'average daily wage penalties' under the Minnesota Payment of Wages Act. It analyzes statutory text distinguishing between rights granted to employees versus enforcement powers granted exclusively to the Commissioner.
subtopics: Statutory construction of Minn. Stat. § 181.171 and § 181.101(a)
The exclusive role of the Commissioner in assessing and collecting penalties under § 181.101
'Know-how' canon: Comparing § 181.101 with other statutes (§§ 181.13, 181.14) where legislatures explicitly authorized private penalty collection
Conclusion: Affirmance of dismissal based on lack of private statutory right

outline.chapter_title: Jurisdictional Crisis: Standing, Mootness, and MFLSA Penalties
outline.description: This critical chapter explores whether Cohen retains Article III standing to pursue statutory penalties under the MFLSA after receiving full compensation for his injuries. It applies Supreme Court precedent regarding voluntary cessation and mootness to determine if a live controversy exists.
subtopics: **Friends of the Earth v. Laidlaw** doctrine: Civil penalties as a remedy for ongoing unlawful conduct vs. past harm
**Town of Chester**: Requirement that standing must persist throughout litigation (mootness)
**Voluntary Cessation Analysis**: Is it 'absolutely clear' that Consilio's overtime policy will not recur?
**Remand Order**: Vacating summary judgment solely to allow the district court to resolve jurisdiction/mootness first

outline.chapter_title: Waiver Issues Regarding MWTA Claims and Injunctive Relief
outline.description: This final chapter addresses two distinct grounds for affirmance: (a) failure to raise a valid legal argument supporting penalties under the Wage Theft Act (MWTA), resulting in waiver; and (b) improper introduction of new requests for injunctive relief via briefing rather than amended pleadings.
subtopics: Failure to argue MWTA penalty authority leads to waiver under **Milligan** standard
Procedural defect in raising new injunctive relief requests in summary judgment briefs
Rule 15(a) requirements for amending complaints vs. opposition briefs
Final disposition: Affirming dismissal on these grounds
